A behavioural test covers a head missing a required context
docs/internal/release-guide.md (probe recovery) names the stale-branch case and its remedy
description:
## Problem
On #4329 (head 964d214ecc, 2026-11-19) `make pr-arm` reported "armed" while the ruleset-required check `release-v2 probe` did not exist on the head commit. The probe dispatch job checks out the PR head and runs that branch's `scripts/release_probe_launch.py`; the branch predated #4379, whose script creates the check run, so no check was ever posted. Auto-merge sat BLOCKED for hours with every reported check green, and re-running the dispatch job could not fix it. Only a develop merge into the branch did. Any open PR whose last develop merge predates #4379 has the same stall.

## Decision gate
Pick one, smallest first:
(a) pr-arm (and pr-landing) list required contexts from the develop ruleset and refuse or warn with a remedy when one is absent and no workflow run that would post it is queued;
(b) the probe dispatch job runs the script from the base branch (`github.event.pull_request.base.sha`) rather than the head;
(c) both. Record the choice and reason in context.

## Guardrails
- Never post the required check from a stand-in or by hand.
- Do not make missing required checks non-blocking.
- Keep the existing pr-arm refusal rules intact.

## Verification rubric
A test reproduces a PR head whose required context is absent and shows pr-arm reporting it with the remedy (merge develop / re-dispatch), or the probe dispatch posts the check for a head whose own script predates the check-creation code.
